messages:
anya: heads-up — ran a focused microbench to repro the p99 spike on Qwen-7B after the int8 kernel swap. looks like KV write/spill is the main culprit.

sam: nice, can you paste the numbers? which sequences and batch sizes?

anya: quick summary: small-batch latency for gen (batch=1) is fine, but when prefix>1024 and batch>4 p99 jumps ~20-25% on INT8. FP8 and fp16 configs not regressing.

lee: that smells like the new reduce kernel we landed last week. maybe it's doing extra copies for KV pages, or misaligned vector stores.

anya: exact microbench output below (trimmed):
```
model: qwen-7b
profile: int8-kernel-v2 (rolled 2026-03-12)
seq/pref: 256 / 2048
batch: 8
p50: 110ms
p95: 240ms
p99: 680ms  <-- before (baseline int8-kernel-v1): 540ms
kv-spill writes: 1.9x higher write time
CPU sys: +12%
GPU compute time: ~same
```

maria: interesting that GPU time unchanged — points to host-side copy/serialize or driver sync. any trace/ flame graphs?

anya: perf-bot collected a small profile for the request path. attaching snippet:

```
# perf-bot summary (top 5 hostside stacks)
1) kv_cache::spill -> memcpy_async -> nvtx_sync
2) batching::prepare_requests -> serialize -> copy_to_device
3) kernel_router::select -> scalar_fallback_path
4) caching::prefix_lookup -> lock_wait (rare)
5) http::encode -> write
```

sam: thanks. so both memcpy_async and nvtx_sync spikes. Could be mis-ordered CUDA events in the int8 path. Do we have a repro that toggles only the kernel variant?

anya: yes — ran same workload with only kernel swapped: int8-v1 (old) vs int8-v2 (new). v2 has higher host-side wait. I can push a small harness to perf infra.

lee: what's the impact across models? only Qwen?

anya: quick cross-model check:
- llama-2-13b: negligible change (~2-3% p99)
- mistral-7b: ~7% p99 increase on long prefixes
- qwen-7b: 18-25% p99 (worst)
so model-specific layout + kv page count seems to amplify it.

maria: ok. this means routing policy could help short-term. we can force qwen->fp8 or int8-v1 on Dedicated for affected customers.

sam: agree. ops question: is int8-v2 enabled as default in the catalog? we rolled it staged but the global flag flipped last night I think.

anya: yes default flipped at ~1768390000. rollout window matches when alerts started.

lee: action items: reproduce on perf infra, bisect kernel change, add nvtx markers around host/device ops, and temporarily pin routing. I'll own kernel bisect.

maria: I'll file a short customer-facing note and run a targeted routing change for Dedicated customers with traffic to qwen-7b. suggested message: "We are temporarily routing Qwen workloads to the FP8 kernel while we investigate an INT8 host-side regression" — ok? :thumbsup:

sam: also add a unit microbench that simulates KV spill pattern (prefix-heavy) so we catch this in CI. we don't have a good prefix-heavy synthetic test.

anya: added a quick config snippet I used for the microbench (can be copied into perf harness):
```json
{
  "model": "qwen-7b",
  "batch_sizes": [1,4,8,16],
  "prompt_prefix_length": [512,1024,2048],
  "tokens_per_request": 512,
  "kernel_variants": ["int8-v1","int8-v2","fp8","fp16"]
}
```

lee: perfect. please also include a per-kernel KV write counters in the returned perf metrics (kv_pages_written, kv_copy_bytes, host_sync_time_ms).

anya: will do. preliminary numbers show kv_copy_bytes up ~2.1x with int8-v2 for qwen-7b with 2048 prefix.

maria: longer-term: probably need model-specific quant profiles that include kernel hints for kv-copy layout or an ABI contract for page alignment. we should add this to the quant profile repo.

sam: agree — add "kv_alignment_hint" to quant profile schema and a recommended fallback kernel. that lets routing pick optimal kernel per model+prefix distribution.

lee: note: we tried a naive kv_alignment_hint before but it was ignored by the runtime. if we formalize it in the profile and plumb it into kernel selection logic we can avoid surprises.

anya: I'm drafting a PR for the quant-profiles repo with entries for qwen/mistral/llama showing tested defaults and fallback list (fp8 first, int8-v1 fallback for qwen). will post link here when ready.

perf-bot: perf test job #3245 finished: qwen-int8-v2 microbench p99 regression reproduced (CI harness). job log: https://perf.redwood/jobs/3245

maria: great. let's keep this thread for progress. next check-in after kernel bisect + routing change. thanks all :heart:
